chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibrahim ibn Uqbah, from Isma'il ibn Sahl and Isma'il ibn 'Abbad, both of them raising it to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
There was none from the children of Adam who was a believer except that he was poor, and no disbeliever except that he was rich, until Ibrahim عليه السلام came and said:
Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve.
So Allah placed among these wealth and need, and among those wealth and need.

key_terms.رَبَّنَا: Our Lord; a direct address in supplication to Allah
key_terms.فِتْنَةً: a trial, test, or means of temptation
key_terms.كَافِرٌ: a disbeliever; one who rejects faith
key_terms.مُؤْمِنٌ: a believer, one characterized by faith

ai.seo_question: Why are both believers and disbelievers found among the rich and the poor?
ai.summary: The hadith states that before the supplication of Ibrahim عليه السلام, believers were characterized by poverty and disbelievers by wealth. After his du'a, Allah caused both wealth and need to exist among both groups, so that material condition would not serve as a decisive trial or sign in itself.
